transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2027-05-05 15:00 UTC
Duration: ~57 minutes
Attendees: Jordan (Redwood AE), Maya (Redwood SE), Sofia (Halcyon Head of Search), Ethan (ML Eng), Liam (CTO)
Shared: deck - /redwood/hosted-vector-demo.pdf, demo notebook - link in chat

[00:00] Jordan: hey everyone, thanks for joining, i think we have like 55 minutes? um we'll run through a hosted embeddings + reranker demo, then show the console and some Optimize recommendations, and leave time for q&a. maya and i will tag in for the technical bits.
[00:18] Sofia: great, thanks. quick context — we're redoing our search stack for halcyon.com, roughly 40 million product + content docs, current stack is a hybrid of elastic + an off-the-shelf vector store. main problems: poor tail relevance and cost spike during sales launches. goal is sub-200ms p95 for user search and better top-3 relevance. timeline is Q3 rollout.
[00:42] Jordan: perfect, that's helpful. maya, want to start with the high level API pattern?
[00:48] Maya: sure. so the hosted flow we usually recommend is two-step: first, call the embeddings endpoint to vectorize queries. second, do a retrieval step against your index (you can use any vector DB), then call our rerank endpoint to score the top-K candidates with context. reranker takes candidate docs + query and returns a scored ordering and optional explanations. it's purpose-built for production — low latency, streaming, and deterministic scoring hooks you can instrument.
[01:15] Ethan: couple quick things — what are typical latencies on hosted for the embedding call and reranker? and cost per 1k requests roughly?
[01:26] Maya: good q. embeddings vary by model but for our medium-size verified model you should expect 20-40ms for a single query embedding in hosted at p50, p95 closer to 80-120ms depending on load. reranker p50 is often 30-80ms for scoring top-10 when using the optimized rerank model. cost depends on token pricing for rerank and per-embedding unit; i'll share a sample pricing sheet but rough hosted numbers for a production profile: embeddings at $0.0008 per vector and rerank at $0.003-$0.01 per call depending on model size.
[02:05] Liam: that matches our expectations. can you talk about batching? we typically have bursts during launches.
[02:12] Maya: yes. Redwood Optimize will recommend batching thresholds based on your traffic distribution — continuous batching at the runtime can group similar short requests to increase throughput and lower per-token cost while holding latency SLOs. in hosted mode we auto-batch small windows, and for Dedicated you can tune batch sizes aggressively. also prefix caching and KV cache for conversational contexts, and key-value cache on the runtime reduces repeated seq work. sometimes the transcript writes kv as key vee cache — just a note that docs use KV cache.
[02:46] Sofia: how deterministic is rerank? we need consistent ordering for A/B tests.
[02:50] Maya: rerank is deterministic per model+seed; we expose rollouts so you can pin a version and run canary or A/B. Console shows model-level metrics, token counts, latency, and per-route cost, so you'll be able to compare before/after easily.
[03:10] Jordan: i'm going to share my screen — we'll hit the API example in the notebook, then the console.
[03:20] [screen share starts]
[03:25] Jordan: here's the notebook. first cell is auth + client. sample call: client.embeddings.create({model: "redwood-embed-med-001", input: "best waterproof jacket"}) — returns a 768-d vector. then we do a candidate fetch from Pinecone (or your index) and then client.rerank.score({model: "redwood-rerank-v2", query: q, candidates: candidates}) — returns scores.
[03:56] Ethan: do you support returning explanations or tokens that influenced the score? we've had regulators ask for traceability for some re-ranks.
[04:05] Maya: yes, we support structured explanations field — a short token-span trace and contribution score. note that for privacy you can disable spans. also Console includes tracing hooks that map request->model->token-count and stores eval traces if you enable them.
[04:28] Liam: security — we are enterprise, need SOC2, SSO/SAML, KMS and VPC options. how does hosted handle keys and logs?
[04:36] Jordan: hosted supports enterprise plan with customer-managed KMS via cloud provider integrations (we can do bring-your-own-KMS in the enterprise offering). we are SOC2 Type II, we provide audit logs, SSO via SAML or OIDC, RBAC at token and route level. for strict data residency or air-gapped needs we recommend Private deployment or Dedicated with VPC. i'll share the security packet after the call.
[05:00] Sofia: good. what about retention? we need 30-day logs and deletion policies for PII.
[05:06] Jordan: you set retention per workspace; default is 90 days for traces but can be shortened. deletion hooks and redaction support exist and we can contract a retention SLA.
[05:18] [06:00] demo continues — Jordan runs a live rerank on a sample query, UI flickers, small stutter noted
[06:05] Maya: note — the small stutter is from my local network; hosted would be steady. live call now: query "best hiking jacket for wet climates" — embeddings call returns vector, retrieval returns 50 candidates, rerank scores top 10 and returns improved ordering with explanation.
[06:40] [08:12] Sofia: the results look pretty good; can we tune the reranker to prefer user reviews and recency? we weight recency heavily for our commerce vertical.
[08:22] Maya: absolutely — rerank can accept feature vectors per candidate (e.g., review_score, recency_days, purchase_velocity) alongside the text and we do a blended scoring model. Optimize will also show model calibration guidance and suggest a lightweight feature join in the candidate payload.
[09:01] Ethan: are there limits on candidate context size? like if each doc is 2k tokens and we pass top-20 that's large.
[09:10] Maya: good point. we recommend truncating to relevant fields and using dense metadata features. our rerank model handles up to ~2048 token context effectively; for larger doc bodies we provide chunking helpers and we support sparse/dense hybrid where chunk-level embeddings feed into rerank with aggregated scoring.
[09:40] Liam: curious about offline evals — can we run batch rerank on historical queries to compute MRR lifts?
[09:48] Jordan: yes, you can call the rerank endpoint in batch mode or use the offline evaluator in Optimize. many customers run a 48-72h offline job against a sample of queries to measure NDCG/MRR before a pilot. we'll share a sample eval harness in the notebook.
[10:12] Maya: also Optimize will recommend model quantization settings — for Halcyon's traffic profile we might suggest int8 quantization for the rerank model to reduce GPU memory and cost, with a small expected quality delta that we track via evaluation prompts.
[10:34] Sofia: can you quantify cost savings? even ballpark percentages?
[10:38] Maya: typical wins from batching + quant + caching are 30-60% unit cost reduction depending on workload. e.g., prefix/KV cache really helps for conversational contexts; for search with high repeat queries batching gives the most gain. we'll run a tailored projection once we have real traffic shape.
[10:58] [12:00] cross-talk about infra details, ember of mis-transcribed words like 'sammel' for SAML occasionally
[12:30] Ethan: technical deep-dive — how do you do fallbacks? if the primary rerank model is busy can we degrade to a cheaper model?
[12:37] Maya: yes, smart routing and fallbacks are built-in. you can define routing policy by latency, cost, region, or tier. a common pattern: try redwood-rerank-v2, fallback to redwood-rerank-small if latency SLO is at risk. the client sees a consistent API and Console shows fallback events.
[13:05] Sofia: what about data exfil concerns — can we prevent copies of docs leaving our environment?
[13:10] Jordan: for highest control we recommend Dedicated or Private deployment. hosted encrypts in transit and at rest; customer-managed KMS ensures we never hold unencrypted keys. we can also sign an addendum limiting model training on customer data — we don't use customer data to continue training without explicit terms.
[13:35] [17:40] demo: show Console - route-level dashboard, token breakdown, cost per route, top-errors, trace detail.
[17:50] Maya: this console view is where your SREs will live — you can slice by token user, model, route, and see per-request trace that maps calls to model kernel choices. we also show recommended batch sizes in Optimize and suggested quant profiles.
[18:22] Ethan: can we integrate console metrics into our Datadog?
[18:27] Jordan: yes, we push events via metrics bridge and have a datadog exporter; we also support Prometheus and direct webhooks for traces.
[18:44] Liam: ok this is all helpful. operational question — for a pilot, what's a minimal scope?
[18:51] Jordan: typical minimal pilot: 1) 1-week live pilot on hosted using a slice of traffic (or replayed queries) 2) run offline eval (48h) against historical queries 3) use Optimize to tune batching/caching and produce a cost projection. success criteria: >10% MRR or DCG improvement and p95 latency <200ms for search endpoints.
[19:18] Sofia: that fits. how soon can we start the pilot?
[19:22] Jordan: we can kick off as soon as we have sample logs and an approved pilot contract. i'll send the pricing+pilot doc today.
[19:30] [29:00] discussion drifts to contract and procurement, typical legal items
[29:12] Liam: procurement will want a data processing addendum and evidence of SOC2.
[29:20] Jordan: noted, we'll attach our SOC2 attestation, security packet, and the DPA template.
[29:30] [40:00] Q&A on edge cases — long docs, multi-lingual embeddings, incremental reindexing
[40:20] Maya: for multi-lingual we have multilingual embeddings and language detection heuristics; for incremental indexing we support delta updates and partial rerun.
[41:05] Ethan: any restrictions on passing customer PII in text fields?
[41:10] Jordan: you control what you send. we recommend tokenizing/redacting PII before calling hosted if you need strict control; otherwise enterprise contracts can specify retention and allowable fields.
[41:32] [50:00] recap and next steps
[50:05] Jordan: recap — Redwood will: 1) send hosted pricing + pilot contract; 2) share demo notebook and offline eval harness; 3) Maya will run a latency/cost projection for Halcyon's 40M docs; 4) Halcyon to send 24h sample query logs and schema. agreed?
[50:31] Sofia: yes. we'll get logs to Ethan and he will upload by Friday.
[50:40] Ethan: yes i can do that.
[50:43] Liam: procurement will review SOC2 and DPA, expect back within 2 weeks.
[50:49] Jordan: great. i'll also include the security packet and a suggested pilot runbook. any final q's?
[51:05] Sofia: one last — can we have a quick 30-min follow-up focused on query log signal engineering? maybe next Tuesday?
[51:13] Jordan: absolutely. i'll propose times.
[51:18] [end transcript meta: occasional mis-transcriptions present; filler words and overlaps retained to match Fireflies style]

Meeting close.
